description: Localized, dependency-driven compiler for permanent L4 product contracts.
principles: The root LLM detects the communication language, translates friendly step titles and creates the visible roadmap before clarification begins.

The runtime prefixes E1-through-E6 and the E8 skeleton checkpoint with the deterministic 👤 marker; dynamically appended technical nodes do not duplicate it, and persisted localized titles remain plain reusable text.
E4 parallel children are dispatched by stable entity: selectors and reconstruct their base invocation when collab-messages omits planning or prompt metadata on materialized fan-out children.

Every E4, E7 and E8 parallel artifact worker submits a strict-tool flexible envelope. The envelope is a valid collab-messages payload, so healthy workers never transiently enter the failed state before their deterministic after-prompt gate runs.
Nested artifact schemas used by a worker tool hoist $defs to the function-parameters root and omit the embedded $id; strict providers resolve root-relative refs from that root.
Dynamic E4 dispatch is symmetric: before-prompt prefers hook args, while after-prompt falls back to the selector retained in step.prompt when collab-messages omits callback args.
E2 normalizes every journey businessObject to one stable PascalCase identifier; E4 consumes that exact id for its entity or projection instead of comparing a localized display label.

E2 treats required as an executable contract: only required entry contexts must be available or located, optional handoffs never become unconditional step prerequisites, and E4 requires ontology coverage only for required contexts.
E2 proposals must pass an independent 🔎 semantic coverage judge before human review; deterministic structural repair and semantic complete-draft repair have separate bounded budgets.

E2 policy decisions are explicit journey contracts: generation declares chosen alternatives without impact, the independent judge adds impact and related journeys, and human selections are preserved in the approved journey index.

A human policy selection different from the generated choice always starts a complete next-round E2 rewrite. A deterministic honor gate rejects a rewritten draft that does not make each selected choice its chosen value.

E2 linear steps cannot combine creation and maintenance when their context preconditions differ; the judge requires separate outcome journeys and repair instructions are placed after the complete draft.

E2 semantic coverage converges through at most three focused patch repairs: omitted contracts remain byte-for-byte equivalent after normalization, each patch passes the complete deterministic gate, and an unchanged blocker set fails early.
E1 preserves its full reviewed contract, supports repeated prompt-driven revisions and only unlocks compilation after the rich deterministic gate passes.
E2 through E6 approval callbacks persist their already-gated permanent review artifacts before adding the result anchor; E7 is an automated compiler after the sixth checkpoint.
Every implemented compile step writes a permanent L4 artifact and a stable result anchor.

Every permanent TypeScript artifact imports its canonical artifact interface from agentNewSolution4/types.ts, is emitted with as const satisfies and exports its exact typeof contract; module, journey, access, ontology and rule shape drift therefore fails tsc while module-specific literal unions remain available without copied strings.
Permanent L4 artifacts plus their approved module checkpoint are the resume authority; pipeline state is monotonic and is reconciled from those artifacts if a late callback lags behind.

A single module-name invocation is canonicalized before the root planner: BuildFlowFsm23 resolves to the existing buildFlowFsm23 folder, so resume never creates a fresh E1 tree before checking pipeline ownership.
A completed result anchor carries the bounded approved contract needed by the immediately unlocked successor, avoiding a storage-index visibility race between client hooks.
Module and index artifacts retain userLanguage and localized stepTitles for maintenance and resume context; per-item E7 artifacts do not repeat it.
Terminal step failures use traceMsg in the task and persist status, error and failedAt in the pipeline whenever a module pipeline already exists.
Previous flow versions are never migrated automatically.
The /fast flag uses the same deterministic gates and persistence paths; E1 auto-accepts its clarification and valid E2-E6 proposals are approved without opening their widgets.

E1 records modernization strategies now; E4 currently compiles only explicit new-solution ontology contracts and fails closed for modernization instead of fabricating a greenfield or replacement database.
E4 classifies every entity into an explicit persistence target: shared MDM for stable base records, module database for transactions, or derived/external/embedded storage for non-table concepts.

Every E4 lifecycle declares its initial state and optional terminal states explicitly; E7 copies that contract mechanically rather than inferring lifecycle meaning from state ordering or missing outgoing transitions.

E4 first freezes a compact ontology overview, then details entities through the proven parallel_dynamic fan-out with maxParallel 20, binds every relationship to exact existing endpoint fields or an explicit non-FK realization, and only then opens one human review.
E2, E3 and E4 carry business-rule references only as stable useRules ids; descriptions exist exactly once in rules/rules.defs.ts.

E5 reconstructs its inputs from approved permanent journey, access and ontology artifacts, collects useRules mechanically and creates one concise rule catalog instead of compiling executable rule objects.

E3, E4 and E5 use one shared approved-artifact reader: journey and ontology indexes plus their per-item defs, and the access-matrix def. Recovery never depends on the large E2/E4 pipeline drafts; E4 entity repair reads only the matching prior entity def.
E5 uses one reasoning call, one deterministic gate and at most one bounded repair. The gate requires every useRules id referenced by E2-E4 to have one description.

E6 is the sixth and final clarification: one conservative reasoning call reviews only justified horizontal modules and external plugins, accepts an empty recommendation list and excludes platform baseline capabilities.
The historical e6-behaviors runtime plan id remains a stable internal identifier; the permanent artifact uses composition terminology and previous flow versions are rejected rather than migrated.
Future pages, use cases, tables and maintenance operations scan the complete L4 and attach only useRules ids; changing a rule description never requires copying text into its consumers.
E7 mechanically groups identical journey step ids into stable N-to-one channel-neutral use cases, details them with a maxParallel 20 fan-out and runs one targeted repair round for invalid drafts.
E7 preserves every journey businessHash and compiles small reusable behaviors with exact context ids, ontology entity refs, behavior-owned rule ids and references to valid lifecycle transitions.

E7 deterministically rejects unreachable lifecycle states, unoperated transitions, dead lifecycle predicates and multi-state entities without workflows; its report presents an explicit human choice to add an upstream E2 operation or shrink the E4 lifecycle, never choosing silently.
Use cases do not copy E3 actors, authorities or scopes and do not prescribe ports, repositories, storage routing or backend architecture. E3 owns authorization and E8 owns channel integration.

E8 derives workspace partition, page context, slices, invalidations, hub candidacy and navigation candidates from approved L4 contracts; its LLM calls may only localize presentation and select a closed surface catalog.

E8 has one human checkpoint for the frozen skeleton. Its workspace-detail fan-out is bounded to 20 workers, validates each worker independently, and writes permanent typed workspace artifacts plus a workspace index.

invocation.resumeRule: A v24-owned incomplete module starts a localized root plan and resumes at the first incomplete implemented step. Module-name lookup accepts an initial-capital or other canonical-equivalent spelling and retains the actual normalized folder name. Previous flow versions are not migrated; foreign or older modules are rejected.

orchestration.treeCreation: after root LLM, before any human clarification
orchestration.roadmapExecution: E9 and later steps remain visible waiting_dependency/manual_later nodes until their implementations are delivered.

steps.goal: Confirm the complete initial product contract: identity, review policy, solution/modernization strategy, business scope, localization and declared constraints.
runtimeNotes: The root plan seeds the localized clarification and the full normalized review is preserved in its answer anchor.
A human change request adds the next open E1 round before completing the current clarification.
Validation failures remain visible inside the same widget and do not mark the step or pipeline failed.
/fast uses the same widget event with autoAcceptSeconds=10.
LLM failures return through afterPrompt and remain visible in the task trace.

steps.goal: Validate and write the initial permanent module contract.
Generate, adjust and approve permanent connected business journeys.
runtimeNotes: prompt_ready preserves the hook args byte-for-byte.
E2 is marked running only after the LLM call returns to afterPrompt.
Terminal failures are persisted in pipeline.steps.e2.error and failedAt.
A deterministic gate failure persists the invalid draft and may schedule one bounded structural repair for the current proposal cycle.
A structurally valid draft is not shown immediately: an independent reasoning-model judge compares all E1 actors, capabilities, screen intents and outcomes with E2.
The generated candidate uses an internal flexible payload so it cannot flash as a human clarification before gate and judge approval.
The coverage judge rejects missing recipient journeys, orphan user outcomes, raw-id risks and human-selectable references without named context acquisition or a credible lookup source.
One complete-draft semantic repair is allowed independently of structural repair; it returns through the gate, is judged again and fails closed if coverage remains incomplete.
An invalid judge envelope is retried once. Compact judge results remain in the task trace after large LLM interactions are cleaned.
Only a judged-complete draft opens the 👤 widget; /fast also waits for the same judgment before durable approval.
Generation declares journey policy decisions before journeys and never supplies impact; the independent judge is the only stage that may add decision impact and related journeys.

Selecting an alternative or requesting free-text changes preserves the current versioned draft, starts a full replacement round, and passes the deterministic selected-choice honor gate before the widget can reopen.

Approval persists every decision selection, including unchanged generated choices, in the journey index. A deterministic E2 impact report records downstream E3-E7 contracts made stale by changed, added or removed journeys.
Prerequisite handoffs use stable context ids exported by the referenced journey.
contextRequired, contextOrLookup and eventDriven declare at least one required entry context; coldStart declares no required entry context.

contextOrLookup includes an explicit locate fallback for every required carried context; optional handoffs may enrich the journey but cannot be an unconditional requiresContext unless an earlier step produces them.
E2 and E4 consume the same shared required-context semantics so an optional handoff cannot become an accidental ontology requirement.
Journey rule references are stored only in business.useRules as lower-camel ids; E2 never copies rule descriptions.

steps.goal: Generate, iteratively adjust and approve the collab-auth access matrix, data scopes and disclosure boundaries.
runtimeNotes: Each human change request adds the next open E3 round before completing the current clarification.
Every round returns to the same localized matrix widget until explicit approval.
Authorities follow the lowercase collab-auth domain:code convention and remain opaque to the agent.
External grants cannot use organization-wide scope.
Limited disclosure records an enforceable projection intent; hiding fields in the frontend is insufficient.
The /fast path validates and approves the same E3 contract without opening the widget.
The e3-result handoff carries the approved review, approval metadata and permanent artifact path for the immediately unlocked E4 hook.
Late or duplicate callbacks cannot regress an approved E3 pipeline state to running, waitingHuman or failed.
Terminal failures are persisted in pipeline.steps.e3.error and failedAt.
Grant rule references are stored only in grants[].useRules; descriptions remain owned by E5.

steps.goal: Generate, directly annotate, structurally adjust and approve the connected greenfield business ontology.
runtimeNotes: The first reasoning call returns only the frozen cross-entity overview: entity identity, source refs, lifecycle states and predicates, MDM/storage routing and relationships; it does not generate fields or rule descriptions.
Before entity fan-out, the overview gate requires every required E2 carried or produced businessObject to exist as an E4 entity or projection with the same id.
One parallel_dynamic child then details each entity with filtered E2/E3 context; maxParallel is 20, matching the proven agentNewSolution ontology implementation.

Parallel children complete with trace on provider or gate failure so one entity cannot fail the fan-out; the deterministic finalizer runs one targeted parallel repair round for only missing or invalid entities.
The finalizer reassembles the unchanged human E4 review contract and reruns the complete journey/access/relationship gate before opening one widget or approving /fast.
The run carries solutionMode=new explicitly; it never infers or fabricates a legacy database contract.
E4 consumes the permanent access/access-matrix.defs.ts artifact; during the immediate E3-to-E4 transition it may consume the identical approved contract carried by e3-result.

Stable base registrations such as clients, projects, regions and material catalogs are proposed as organization-scoped MDM; orders, movements, logs, invoices and other transactions use the module database.
Master data and operational state are separate entities: a Material catalog may be MDM while inventory balance, adjustment and usage remain transactional.
Every entity carries a structured storage target, scope, identifier and MDM type when applicable; the ontology index repeats this compact persistence routing for L1/L2 compilers.

Static field constraints are shared validation contracts: backend enforcement is mandatory and frontend mirrors them for early feedback. Named lifecycle meanings required by sources are frozen as exact lifecycle predicate-to-state mappings; dynamic, time-relative, cross-entity and authorization conditions remain E5 rules.
Every non-empty lifecycle declares one initialState and may declare terminalStates; the E4 gate verifies membership and rejects an initial state marked terminal.
The review widget groups entities by persistence destination and highlights cross-store relationships before approval.
The review widget separates safe direct title/description edits from structural LLM requests.
Before a structural revision, the current draft including direct human edits is persisted and supplied to the next round.
A first deterministic gate failure persists the draft and schedules one bounded LLM repair step before failing the task.
Every E2 journey, now feature and E3 information authority remains traceable from the ontology.
After entity fan-out, one compact reasoning pass binds every semantic relationship to exact existing endpoint fields, or explicitly declares an MDM/derived realization without a fake foreign key.
The binding gate rejects missing relationships, invented fields, endpoint drift and persistence-strategy mismatches; one localized binding repair is allowed before failure.
Relationships must preserve selected business context so later screens never require typed foreign-key ids.
Approval writes one permanent defs file per entity plus a small ontology index with the frozen hash.
Each human change request adds the next open E4 round before completing the current clarification.
Terminal failures persist the invalid draft when available and pipeline.steps.e4.error/failedAt.
Entity rule references are stored only in useRules; static field constraints remain typed data validation contracts rather than catalog business rules.

steps.goal: Create one human-readable source of truth for every business-rule id referenced by L4.
runtimeNotes: prompt_ready preserves the original hook args byte-for-byte so proposal and repair stages cannot lose their round identity.
The runtime mechanically collects the unique useRules ids present in approved journeys, access grants and ontology entities.
One reasoning call receives those ids and compact approved L4 context, then returns only id and one precise human-readable description per rule.
The deterministic gate rejects duplicate or invalid ids and any referenced id without a description; unrelated catalog rules are allowed for future consumers.
One transport retry and one deterministic-gate repair are bounded; E5 has no per-rule fan-out, executable policy schema or independent judge.
Static scalar field constraints remain in E4 and are not duplicated as business rules.
A human change request persists the edited draft and adds the next open E5 round before completing the current clarification.
Approval writes one rules/rules.defs.ts catalog and an approved review snapshot for future maintenance and L1/L2 compilation.
Later page, use-case, table and behavior compilers scan the complete L4 for matching rule ids and store only useRules references.

steps.goal: Conservatively review whether realization needs an additional horizontal business module or external plugin.
runtimeNotes: This is the sixth and final human clarification before realization.
One compact reasoning call consumes approved E1, journeys, ontology and rules; fields and access details are omitted from the prompt.
An empty recommendation list is valid and preferred when approved L4 has no evidence for an addition.
Authentication/RBAC, i18n, tenant isolation, files, LLM proxy, messages/tasks, monitoring and auditing are platform baseline and cannot become recommendations.
Recommendations contain only id, kind, title, purpose and include/defer decision; implementation design is deferred to E7.
One transport retry and one deterministic-gate repair are bounded; there is no fan-out or independent judge.
A human may approve immediately or request another conservative proposal through the same localized 6/6 widget.
The stable e6-behaviors runtime id is internal; only modules owned by the current flow version may resume.

steps.goal: Compile approved journeys into small channel- and architecture-neutral business behaviors and lifecycle workflows.
runtimeNotes: The plan is mechanical: identical stable step ids converge into one use case and every journey step remains covered through compiledFrom.
One parallel_dynamic reasoning child describes each behavior from filtered journey, ontology and rule context; maxParallel is 20.
Context requires/provides are exact E2 ids; context lineage remains compiled mechanically in journey realization instead of being copied into use cases.
E5 rules are candidates and the use case references only rules enforced by its own behavior.
Draft contract versions are explicit. A resume reuses only drafts from the current simple contract and never migrates the previous oversized shape silently.
The gate validates descriptions, exact E2 contexts, E4 entity refs, existing E5 ids and valid lifecycle transitions; field selection and persistence are not part of the use-case contract.

Actors, authorities and scopes remain in E3; inputs, outputs, errors, pagination, selection, projections and route binding remain in E8 or downstream generation; ports, transactions and adapters are implementation choices.

A deterministic finalizer records every gate issue in e7-validation-report.json, repairs only invalid or missing use cases once, derives workflows, writes typed permanent artifacts and advances to E8.
Workflow finalization requires a workflow only for lifecycles with an intermediate state outside initialState and terminalStates; binary inactivation or reversal flags remain valid without one.
A missing workflow suppresses same-entity unreachable and predicate findings. Predicate reachability includes initialState and transition targets.
Lifecycle findings are persisted with explicit operateState (E2) or shrinkLifecycle (E4) choices and open a human resolution checkpoint; they never retry an LLM or fail the task.
Full transitions live only in workflow artifacts; use cases and journeys keep transition refs. Global source hashes, language and timestamps live only in indexes.
Journey business blocks and businessHash values are immutable; E7 writes only resolution/realization metadata.
E7 has no routine human checkpoint. E6 remains the sixth and final product-design clarification; lifecycle findings open only their explicit E2/E4 resolution checkpoint.

steps.goal: Derive, review and compile access-aware workspaces with one composed view call per workspace.
runtimeNotes: Code derives the complete workspace partition, context catalog, hub ranking, candidate edges, hosted use cases and scenario ids from approved E2 through E7 artifacts.

One small reasoning call may localize labels, group already-derived workspaces under existing E2 features, order menu items and select only queueAction, contextualModal or batchAction surfaces; it cannot create, remove or rename structural ids.

The skeleton gate requires total use-case coverage, non-empty workspaces, resolvable page context, collection and record scenarios for a hub, reachable FSM evidence for queues and at most seven menu items per section.
The human checkpoint reviews the map: header links, feature menu, workspaces, scenarios, profiles and context-carrying candidate edges. A requested change starts the next skeleton round.

After approval, one dynamic worker per workspace returns organisms, ontology field projections and command inputs. Each worker is isolated and receives at most one targeted repair round; maxParallel is 20.
Workers cannot change the frozen skeleton. The deterministic detail gate rejects unknown fields, slice/entity drift, unresolved pageContext or selection input, and fieldsOnly disclosure violations.
The finalizer stamps picker use, derives command invalidations from command/slice entity intersections and writes typed workspace defs plus index. E9 owns route and global navigation compilation.
